初學者先以一手握持竹框底部，另一手搖動樂器，使竹管發出共振音；每個音高通常由一支: A beginner holds the bottom of the bamboo frame in one hand and shakes the instrument with the other so that the tubes resonate; each pitch is usually the responsibility of one angklung, so practise the timing of the shake and the stop, play only your own notes in the ensemble, and come in on the beat of the others, and together you make a complete melody. The instrument is an idiophone, sounding class 112.122, from the Sunda region of Indonesia.

安克隆竹琴常見於印尼巽他社群的合奏與儀式場合。演奏者一手握框、一手搖動，每人通常: The angklung is common in the ensembles and ceremonies of Sundanese communities in Indonesia. The player holds the frame in one hand and shakes with the other; each person is usually responsible for one note, and interlocking playing builds the melody. It is traditionally used for rice growing, prayer and celebrations, and also appears in processions, entertainment and education; today it can be retuned to the diatonic scale and played alongside Western instruments.
安克隆竹琴是印尼巽他族的體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號112.1: The angklung is an idiophone of the Sundanese people of Indonesia, Hornbostel–Sachs 112.122. A bamboo frame holds several bamboo tubes, cut so that they sound a pitch and tuned in octaves. The player holds the bottom of the frame in one hand and shakes the instrument with the other, making the tubes sound repeatedly; in an ensemble each person usually has only one note and they shake in turn to build the melody. The instrument has long been used in the ceremonies and farming occasions of Sundanese communities and needs several people to work together.
安克隆竹琴的發聲體與框架均為竹材：由數目不等的竹管附著於竹框，竹管經雕刻以產生共: Both the sounding tubes and the frame are bamboo: an unequal number of tubes is attached to a bamboo frame, the tubes cut to produce a resonating pitch and tuned in octaves. It is played by holding the bottom of the frame in one hand and shaking with the other; the source does not state the species of bamboo, the wall thickness, how the frame is joined or the materials of other parts, so no guess is made.
安克隆竹琴起源於今西爪哇與萬丹，由巽他族長期演奏。印度教時期與巽他王國時期，它用: The angklung comes from what is now West Java and Banten and has long been played by the Sundanese. In the Hindu period and the Sunda Kingdom it was used in ritual honouring the rice goddess, and also for prayer and for music before battle. The oldest surviving example is the seventeenth-century angklung Gubrag of Bogor, and the oldest tradition is the angklung buhun of Lebak in Banten. In 1938 Daeng Soetigna rebuilt it in the diatonic scale, which brought it back into fashion for education, entertainment and the orchestra; it was performed at the 1955 Bandung Conference, and in 1966 Udjo Ngalagena opened the Saung Angklung Udjo. In 2010 it was inscribed on the UNESCO list of intangible cultural heritage.
安克隆竹琴音色清脆明亮，具有獨特的竹質溫潤感。其發聲時帶有輕盈飄然的質感，音域多: The angklung's timbre is crisp and bright, with the distinctive warmth of bamboo. It sounds light and buoyant, mostly in the middle and upper range, and carries well, so it stands out clearly in a band. Because the tubes resonate, shaking produces a layered resonance, a soft sound that is still lively. Against the dry attack of the xylophone it is warmer; against the glockenspiel it lacks the metallic sheen but has more organic naturalness. Its characteristic shake gives the timbre a wave-like quality and creates a relaxed, cheerful atmosphere, and it is often used in folk music for exactly that.
